subject: Request: Approve Variant Downgrade for p95 Tail Discrepancy (Model PHI-2)
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@finnova.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Cc: support@finnova.com
Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden p95 increase on PHI-2 — need guidance

Hi Kimberly,

We're seeing a sustained p95 latency jump on Model PHI-2 for our production traffic starting ~08:40 PST this morning. Our customers on payment flows are reporting timeouts on a small but significant fraction of requests (~1.8% became >1200ms; baseline is ~320ms). Attached is our internal SLO snapshot and the token-size distribution during the window.

Can Redwood advise on an immediate mitigation? We're ok with a temporary performance/carveout if it avoids customer impact, but want the least-risk approach. If a variant switch or rollback to PHI-2-repr-v1 is the recommended action, we need Redwood to approve and run it.

Elena
Director, Payments Engineering
Finnova

Attachments: finnova_slo_report_20290614.pdf

From: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@finnova.com>, support@finnova.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2029 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 increase on PHI-2 — need guidance

Thanks for the data, Elena — sorry you're hitting this. Quick summary of what we're seeing on our side:
- PHI-2 baseline is healthy; an anomalous tail emerged coincident with a canary of PHI-2-repr-v2 (quantized) that rolled at 08:30.
- Canary metrics show a small increase in p95 under longer sequences and high-concurrency bursts.

Two immediate mitigation options:
1) Roll traffic off the v2 variant back to v1 (variant downgrade/rollback). Fastest path to reduce p95 but incurs short routing churn.
2) Activate a provisional SLO carveout and enable aggressive batching/circuit-breaker for Finnova traffic while engineering investigates. Slower to materialize but avoids variant churn.

Requesting internal approval to execute option (1) to minimize customer impact. Ben and Priyom — can you confirm if a variant switch is safe for Finnova's pinned model config (no custom layers)? If yes, I'll ask operations to perform the downgrade and notify Elena.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0138

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2029 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 increase on PHI-2 — need guidance

Kimberly — quick engineering check: we've verified the canary logs and KV cache hit-rate dropped ~6% on v2 when sequences exceed 600 tokens; quantization path is introducing micro-variance in attention kernel that amplifies under multi-request concurrency.
Operational notes:
- Rolling traffic back to PHI-2-repr-v1 is low-risk for Finnova: their model config is standard (no custom ops), traffic can be shifted within a single routing change.
- We should run a short health-check plan post-switch for 30 minutes and keep an emergency revert window of 90 minutes.
- I'll attach a quick perf diff.

Attachment: variant_perf_diff.csv

Priyom — if you can bless the downgrade workflow, we should proceed with Kim's permission.

— Ben
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@finnova.com>, support@finnova.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2029 17:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 increase on PHI-2 — need guidance

Elena — thanks for the patience. After internal ops triage and an engineering check, Redwood recommends a controlled variant downgrade to PHI-2-repr-v1 now. Plan below:

Planned action (ETA: 30 minutes after approval):
- Switch routing for Finnova's instance to PHI-2-repr-v1 (single-step routing change).
- Post-switch health-check: monitor p95, error-rate, and token throughput for 30 minutes.
- If p95 returns to baseline, we keep v1 for Finnova and start a rollback root-cause investigation.
- Emergency revert window: 90 minutes. If the downgrade introduces regressions, we'll revert to v2 and open a support ticket with Finnova and their engineering lead.

We need explicit approval to execute the switch. Please reply with a one-line approval ("Approve switch to PHI-2-repr-v1 now") or request the alternate carveout. Once Elena approves, Ops will run the change and I'll post updates to the HubSpot deal and the runbook link below.

Runbook: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/model-fallback
Deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/8471

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
